Limits The framework has limits, and the chapter insists that users state them clearly
Common failure modes One failure mode is false precision
A neat diagram can make weak evidence look stronger than it is
Another is summary drift, where repeated compression strips away qualifiers until a tentative statement sounds universal
A third is category error: readers sometimes apply a framework built for diagnosis to a context that requires negotiation or experimentation instead
The method is most reliable when the subject has enough stability for concepts to transfer across cases
mechanisms_or_explanations: A structured process can reduce confusion, but it cannot remove disagreement when people have different values, incentives, or risk tolerances
The method is most reliable when the subject has enough stability for concepts to transfer across cases
It is less reliable when the environment changes quickly, because the relationships that explained yesterday's result may not explain tomorrow's
